common_mistakes.mistake: Pac reaches HOLD LIFT before Isp boards the stationary lift, so the lift leaves without him.
common_mistakes.consequence: Isp remains below; the simple order-dependent route has to wait for the lift to cycle back before he can board.
common_mistakes.recovery: Keep Pac on the pad, let Isp wait on the dock, board on the returning lift, then carry him up; the authored hint gives this recovery and a native replay completes it after an early activation.

evidence.claim: Authored hint explicitly describes waiting for the lift to return and boarding.
The returning-cycle native replay completes both exits after early activation; it demonstrates feasibility, not human recovery success.

common_mistakes.mistake: Pac steps off HOLD LIFT before Isp boards or transfers to the upper tissue.
common_mistakes.consequence: Lift loses power and may descend; Isp may have to wait and reboard, repeating travel.
common_mistakes.recovery: Return Pac to the pad and maintain the hold until Isp reaches the upper tissue; the short-release route demonstrates recovery from an early pad release.

common_mistakes.mistake: The intended Gem step is missed or Gem is not displaced to the dock.
common_mistakes.consequence: Pac cannot take the direct expected jump onto the middle tissue, creating a route blockage if the pair assumes Gem is the only step.
common_mistakes.recovery: Isp can serve as a headstep and Pac can reach the same tissue; thereafter the pad/lift route is feasible. This alternate recovery requires a nonobvious cooperative repositioning.

common_mistakes.mistake: Cana’s boomerang hits Pac while he holds on the pad.
common_mistakes.consequence: Pac is shoved off the pad temporarily, stopping lift power and potentially exposing Isp to a missed cycle; the continuous floor avoids a lethal fall in the demonstrated cases.
common_mistakes.recovery: Move back onto the pad and resume holding; if Isp misses the lift, use the returning-cycle recovery. Opening-miss probe also finds a leftward pad position that maintains occupancy while avoiding the projectile lane.

reasoning.rationale: The standard Gem route requires positioning the movable step, then sequencing Isp boarding before Pac powers the lift, transferring Isp to upper tissue before Pac leaves the pad. The alternate route can bypass the Gem setup only through a new cooperative headstep. These are multiple route dependencies, but no novice evidence shows which route players discover.

evidence.claim: The intended sequence and separate platforms/exits are explicit in source; source does not prove first-time comprehension.
Trace realizes the board-before-power dependency.
An alternate recovery works after missed setup.

cooperation.rationale: Both heroes have indispensable differentiated work: Isp moves Gem and must board first; Pac alone can sustain the lift while Isp rides; they then separate to different exits. This is a meaningful handoff and role transfer, not repeated simultaneous precision.

evidence.claim: Hint, Pac-only pad, and distinct exits encode both roles.
Pac holds while Isp rides upward.

execution.rationale: Several controlled actions are required for both heroes: push/jump with a movable body, climb to the middle tissue, board a moving lift under a held state, transfer to upper tissue, then make a long lower return. The scripted route confirms the sequence is physically feasible, not how often novices miss it.

evidence.claim: Platforms at separated heights and both exit routes.
Isp completes upper transfer.
Pac completes lower return.

timing.rationale: The lift cycles and must be boarded before the pad powers it, but it is repeatable and the authored recovery permits waiting for its return. Attacks have windup/cooldown but do not force a narrow chained window in the demonstrated routes.

evidence.claim: Lift is periodic; hint gives a wait-and-reboard fallback; attackers have windup and cooldown.
A missed cycle is recoverable in a completed ordinary-input replay.

hazards.rationale: No meaningful physical danger is established on the mandatory route: although Cana can shove Pac off the pad, the level provides continuous safe_floor below the platforms and authors no lethal hazards. The shove can interrupt lift power or require reboarding, which belongs in execution/recovery rather than hazards.

evidence.claim: The level has continuous safe_floor, no authored hazards, and a pad-triggered boomerang.

novelty.rationale: The powered lift/hold and cooperative role split transfer from levels 01 and 04. Moving Gem provides one supported step route; when that is missed, the separate Isp headstep recovery is a new, source-unestablished application. Neither option is proven first-time discoverable.

recovery_cost.rationale: A missed boarding cycle can require waiting and repeating part of the lift ride; early pad release can interrupt it. Both are recoverable without full reset. Missing the Gem has an alternate headstep route, but discovering it is not guaranteed and may add substantial repositioning.

evidence.claim: Hint describes wait/return/reboard recovery.

solution_clarity.rationale: The captured screenshot shows “Make a step, share the lift, split the route,” the START: HOLD LIFT and PAC HOLD LIFT labels, NO POWER, and separated exits. The locked first-encounter record says those cues identify the lift/step roles but leave the order and meaning of “share” uncertain. They support moderate burden (2): the route’s parts are named, while the causal handoff remains to infer. The optional hint is not part of this clarity estimate.

evidence.claim: Captured subtitle and labels name the lift, step, split route, and separate exits.

control_friction.rationale: No direct two-human input reliability or simultaneous-keyboard evidence is available. Scripted input and browser completion cannot establish shared-keyboard friction.

confidence_reason: Current source clearly defines the legal route and mandatory mechanics; ordinary-input deterministic traces cover the normal route, missed Gem, early pad release, and missed lift cycle, with a final browser receipt for missed-step and missed-cycle completion. These show feasible routes and recovery, not actual novice discovery, frequency, comfort, or shared-keyboard reliability.

confirmed: The subtitle and labels correctly suggested a shared lift, step, split route, differentiated hero roles, and a meaningful causal action.
The idle-based uncertainty about movement, hazards, recovery, and feedback was appropriate at that stage; scripted route evidence now fills mechanics/feasibility but not human outcomes.
missed_mechanics: The pad is Pac-only and powers the lift only while occupied; Isp must board while it is stationary before Pac holds it.
Gem displacement is one supported route to Pac’s tissue, not a strict requirement; the missed-Gem probe completes through an Isp headstep instead.
The pad starts both villain attacks; Cana can shove Pac off the hold, but the continuous floor supports recovery.
The lift can leave without Isp and return; waiting/reboarding is an authored recovery.
Level 37 introduces recoil-driven launch and lower regroup, not a stationary-hero headstep; the missed-Gem headstep is a new recovery application.
changed_judgments: Reasoning moves from 2 to 3 because the source/route establishes a mandatory dependent order (step setup, board, power, transfer, release), beyond the single causal choice visible at idle.
Cooperation moves from 2 to 3 because both distinct contributions and the board-before-hold handoff are confirmed mandatory.
Execution moves from 2 to 3 because the route entails multiple controlled jumps/pushes and both a lift transfer and long split returns; this remains an expert estimate, not measured performance.
Timing becomes 1 rather than unknown because periodic lift boarding is repeatable and missed cycles can be waited out; no narrow active window is required.

Hazards changes from unknown to 0 because source defines no authored hazards and provides continuous safe_floor; the pad-triggered shove creates route disruption/recovery burden, not established physical danger under the rubric.
Novelty remains 2: the powered lift/hold and role split transfer from earlier rooms, while the Gem step is only one route and the alternate headstep recovery is a new, unestablished technique.
Recovery cost becomes 2 because early activation/pad release can repeat part of the route, but the lift return, pad reactivation, and headstep allow recovery without reset.
Clarity remains 2: visible headline/pad labels and explicit hint support understanding, but exact dependency and a Gem-miss recovery are not fully conveyed by the idle cue.

The normal trace’s Gem displacement is one supported route, not a mandatory mechanic: the alternate missed-Gem probe completes both exits without displacing Gem. Level 37’s recoil launch is related cooperation but does not establish the stationary headstep recovery.
unresolved: No first-time pair has been observed; trace feasibility does not show whether they discover the Gem-step route or the novel headstep recovery.
No human two-person control reliability/friction evidence exists.
How often Cana/Gem interference disrupts an unassisted first attempt and how players interpret its feedback remain unknown.

single_operator_note: One person controlling both heroes would need to alternate movement/jump inputs while maintaining Pac on HOLD LIFT and moving Isp; simultaneous hold-plus-traverse may add input switching. No one-operator play was observed, so this remains a note outside the two-human scores.
